title: The session K that drives keyframe selection depends on the card's total memory and on co-tenants, because they set how the 16 probe frames are split into DA3 windows
mechanism: The DA3 probe splits its 16 frames into windows of n_win = window_size(...). n_win comes from the card's TOTAL memory and the 2-frame footprint calibration, and focal.py:123 halves it on an OOM. DA3 predicts each view's K from all views in its window (with the reference-view reordering of M-02), so a different split gives a different per-frame K and a different median K. That K is the only GPU-derived input to I1: it sets the rotation reference H=K R K^-1, so it moves every parallax reading and, through intake-02, the whole keyframe and witness list. Three cases: (1) pccr on the A100 80 GB runs one window of 16 ('predicted peak 44.2 GiB of 80.0'). On the RTX A6000 that CLAUDE.md names, budget = 47.99*0.85-6.36 = 34.4 GiB and 2.365 GiB/frame give 14, so windows [14,2]. (2) zaragoza at 1932 px: 6 on the A100 (windows [6,6,4]), 3 on the A6000. (3) Any co-tenant that causes an OOM halves the split ([8,8]). The only guard before the probe is stop_semantic_service_verified, which checks vLLM and nothing else. None of these items is in the 63: M-01, omega-05 and f0f4-01 cover the I3/gauge windows, not this probe.

focal.py:86  n_win = window_size(..., requested=len(files), ...)
focal.py:94  windows = [[...files[a:a + n_win]] for a in range(0, len(files), n_win)]
log: '[intake.vram] window 16 → 6 frame(s): sized on the card's 80.0 GiB total, 10,764 tokens/frame at process_res 1932' then '[intake.focal] ... fx 2255.83 fy 1699.49'
fix_idea: Make the probe layout independent of the card. Fix it per (model, process_res) in the repo, for example 2-frame windows (the calibration size, which fits anywhere the native resolution can run at all), and use it on every card. On OOM, fail and declare it, never halve. Call require_exclusive_gpu before the probe. Stamp focal_probe.json with card_identity, dtype, weights sha and versions, and refuse when the card differs instead of quietly re-measuring a different K.
skeptic_reason: focal.py:86 sizes the probe windows with window_size(..., requested=16). That function (vram.py:200-204) uses the card's TOTAL memory and the cached footprint. focal.py:123-125 halves n_win on OOM_EXIT. The only guard before the probe is map_worker.py:1793-1795, stop_semantic_service_verified, which checks for 'vllm serve' PIDs and nothing else. Point 5/41 of the plan pins the I3 window, not this probe. The logs show the split is reproducible on one card: pccr 08-31 got fx 387.52 three times from 1 window of 16, and zaragoza got fx 2255.83 three times from 3 windows of ≤6. So the split depends on the card and, through an OOM, on co-tenants.
skeptic_correction: Two more paths make it worse. (1) The halving loop goes down to n_win=1 (`max(1, n_win // 2)`). The probe then becomes 15 single-frame windows plus one 2-frame window, which is single-view DA3 K: a different instrument, not just a different split. (2) The fold rule at focal.py:95-96 merges a lone last frame into the previous window. For 16 frames and n_win ∈ {3, 5, 15}, the last window becomes n_win+1, which is above what window_size sized for the card. Example: an A6000 at 1932 px gives n_win=3 and windows [3,3,3,3,4]. That last window can OOM and start the halving. The A6000 numbers in the finding are arithmetic, not observed.

title: I1 is a sequential chain of hard bars, and each keyframe becomes the next anchor, so one flipped decision re-routes every later keyframe
mechanism: Every window applies hard bars to measured floats: the close test (parallax > hi), band membership (lo <= p <= hi), argmax of sharp_rank in the band, track death at fb <= 1.0 px (a track that fails once is dead for the whole window), a lost frame at < 40 tracks, a lost frame when TRF hits max_nfev=200 at tol 1e-12, the witness bar (>= 1.5 px), and in I0 the exposure bounds (luma 40/220, clip 0.25) that define the chain. The chosen keyframe becomes the next anchor, and select_witnesses chains the same way. A flip in one window therefore changes all later anchors, keyframes, witnesses, I3 windows, the covis plan and Omega. On one node and stack the chain is reproducible: two replace-ON pccr 08-31 runs both gave 289 keyframes and 2100 witnesses with the same K, and the CPU kernels were verified clean. Any upstream bit change does move it: K (intake-01), decoded pixels (intake-04) or library versions (intake-11). Estimate: about 1.2 px of parallax per frame and about 5 frames in the band, so a 0.1 px shift in the readings flips a close or edge in roughly 15 % of windows. With 289 windows a different list is almost certain. Not checked on session data (read-only).
evidence:
parallax.py:509  if m.parallax_px > hi: band = [s for s in seen if lo <= s.parallax_px <= hi]
parallax.py:532  anchor, anchor_is_kf = chosen.frame, True
parallax.py:412-416  ok &= ... (fb <= cfg.fb_max_px); self.alive[idx[~ok]] = False
fix_idea: First remove the upstream variance (intake-01, -04, -11). Then apply 'smoothest option within 2x the measured error'. Measure each reading's error with a fixed-key bootstrap of the 0.9-quantile over the tracks. Close a window only when p > hi + 2e. Take the keyframe as the sharpest I0 frame (sharp_rank does not depend on K) among frames with lo - 2e <= p <= hi + 2e, so the choice rests on the K-free ranking and not on where the bar is crossed. Record each window's margins in selected_frames.json (closing p - hi, band-edge distances, gap between the top-2 sharp_ranks, worst fb margin, TRF nfev) so any remaining flip is visible.
skeptic_reason: select_keyframes (parallax.py:487-537) closes each window on hard bars: p > hi, the lo..hi band, and argmax of sharp_rank. It then makes the chosen frame the next anchor (line 532). select_witnesses (541-561) re-anchors on every chosen witness. Tracks die permanently at fb > fb_max_px=1.0 (line 412-416). A frame is lost at < min_tracks=40, or when TRF stops at max_nfev=200 (status <= 0, line 328). So one flipped decision re-routes every later anchor. The run is reproducible on the same stack: BLAS is limited to 1 thread, ties break by (sharp_rank, -frame), and the logs show 289/2100 repeated.
skeptic_correction: The ~15 %-of-windows flip estimate is not measured. The mechanism only amplifies upstream bit changes: K (intake-01), decoded pixels (intake-04), library versions (intake-11), and a different frame inventory (missed item on truncated extraction). The chain itself is deterministic.

title: Intake markers and the focal-probe cache are reused on keys with no code, library, weights or card identity, and frames are identified by size only
mechanism: With replace OFF, I0 is skipped when the frame names+sizes, params and a hand-bumped QUALITY_VERSION match. I1 is skipped when those match plus the I0 digest, K and a hand-bumped PARALLAX_VERSION. focal_probe.json is reused when {window paths, process_res, model_id string} match. None of these keys includes a git hash of server/intake, the extract_da3_depth/DA3 code, the weights revision or sha, torch/cuDNN/driver, OpenCV/numpy/scipy versions or the card. Frame content is identified by byte size only, never hashed. So a resumed session keeps keyframes and a K computed by older code, libraries or another card, while a fresh replace-ON run recomputes them and can differ (intake-01/02/11). output/salad_revisit_reference.json is also reused by existence whenever walk_is_current holds. omega-21 covers this for the I3 windows, walk and covis, but not for focal, I0 or I1.

title: Frames are decoded and re-encoded by whatever OpenCV/FFmpeg/libjpeg is installed, with no stamp, and the upload never clears an earlier video's frames
mechanism: _extract_video_frames_sync decodes with cv2.VideoCapture. The installed build bundles avcodec 59.37 and swscale 6.7, does YUV to BGR with OpenCV's default SWS_BICUBIC (no +bitexact/+accurate_rnd, so the converter's SIMD path depends on the CPU), and applies rotation by default as that OpenCV version does. It then re-encodes JPEG q95 with the bundled libjpeg-turbo 3.0.3. The same video on another install, or re-uploaded after an OpenCV upgrade, can give different pixels, which change I0 values, the exposure flags and the I1 chain (intake-02). No manifest records the video sha, the decoder or encoder versions, or per-frame hashes. Separately, the upload endpoint neither clears frames/ nor refuses a session that already has frames. Higher-index frames from an earlier, longer video survive, and replace never deletes frames. A second source_video.<ext> can sit beside the first, and precision/camera.find_source_video picks alphabetically. list_frames also accepts two files with the same number (000001.jpg and 000001.png). Their order then comes from iterdir, and _Frames keeps the last one.

main.py:1755  cv2.imwrite(str(frames_dir / f"{idx:06d}.jpg"), frame, params)

fix_idea: Extract with a pinned ffmpeg (declared version) using -sws_flags +bitexact+accurate_rnd+full_chroma_int, an explicit rotation policy and lossless PNG output (or a pinned encoder). Write frames/manifest.json with the video sha256, decoder and encoder versions, flags and per-frame sha256, and use it as the intake's input identity. Refuse an upload into a session that has frames, or replace the frames and the old video atomically. Refuse duplicate frame numbers.

No manifest records the video sha, the codec versions or per-frame hashes. upload_video (1771-1822) writes source_video{ext} and extracts into frames/ without clearing it or refusing a session that already has frames. The replace wipe (pipeline_manager.py:668-676) keeps every frame image. find_source_video (precision/camera.py:578-585) picks alphabetically among source_video.*. list_frames (quality.py:138-151) sorts on int(stem) only, so duplicate numbers keep iterdir order, and _Frames (parallax.py:684) keeps the last one.
skeptic_correction: A decoder version change can also change the frame COUNT or numbering (EOF flush, MP4 edit-list and start-PTS handling, the default auto-rotation). That renumbers every frame, so keyframe ids change, not only pixels. The stale-frames path needs a direct API call, because the UI shows '+' only for sessions without frames.

title: I3 reads its intake parameters from config.yaml as it is on disk when the worker spawns, not from the run's config snapshot
mechanism: main.py builds the run config from config.cfg, which the backend loaded at startup and never reloads. run_da3_windows and walk_is_current instead call load_intake_config(config.cfg) inside the spawned worker (spawn context), which re-reads config.yaml from disk at that moment. The I3 window sizing (vram_calibration_frames, vram_margin_frac) can therefore come from a different config than the focal probe, I1 (whose params_hash records the snapshot) and Omega's margin (map_worker uses _lic(config)). The result depends on whether config.yaml was edited after the backend started, which happens often while other agents edit the repo. Lazy imports inside functions (from intake.walk import ...) likewise load whatever code is on disk at first use, so one run can mix code versions. The same pattern exists in precision/depth_on_f5.py:364/508, corrected_cloud.py:615 and depth_sweep.py:1029 (other slices).

main.py:7736  _run_cfg = dict(cfg)   # cfg imported at backend start

title: Geometric revisit labels are hard bars on I3-derived medians, and the SALAD non-local band is a ceil() of the measured walk
mechanism: intake/walk.revisit_reference sets dist_bar_m = median of the per-window median DA3 depths and cos_bar = cos(half the median HFOV). calibrate_threshold labels a keyframe pair a revisit iff D < dist_bar_m AND F·F > cos_bar. Pairs near either bar flip label, which moves the Youden-J argmax (omega-16 covers the argmax, not these labels) and so the SALAD bar, the candidates, the bridges and the judge count. map_worker also sets the non-local band to ceil(min_walk_m / (walk_m / n_kf)) from the I3 walk, an integer that flips near whole numbers. That ceil is idle on pccr only because min_gap = 20 dominates (17 vs 20).

map_worker.py:2374  _band = max(int(_sal["min_gap"]), int(_math.ceil(_visit_m / (_walk0 / _n_selected))))
fix_idea: Apply the 2x-error rule. Measure each bar's error with a fixed-key bootstrap of the median over windows, and add the walk's seam error to D. Leave out of both classes any pair within 2x that error of either bar. Persist the labels and the calibrated bar with the walk stamp. Take the band as the smallest integer whose walk length clears min_walk_m by 2x the measured walk error, and record the margin.

Both come from medians at walk.py:454-456, and the Youden argmax follows from those labels. map_worker.py:2373-2374 sets the band to ceil(min_walk_m / (walk/n)). The logs confirm the band is then raised to the bridge window: 'floor 17, 0 x 289 frames, one bridge window 20' (pccr); 'floor 20 ... 1998 frames ... 20' (pccr 2408, exactly at the tie).

title: In chunked-metric mode the verifier's residual s is applied to every point with no significance test, and the run is failed or orientation refused on hard bars
mechanism: (a) In chunked-metric mode scale_align is described as the verifier, yet run() always calls apply_scale(s) on chunk PLYs, aligned depth and every camera_poses.txt. No test checks that s differs from 1 beyond its own noise (the user's rule: significant at 95 %, >= 5 judges, >= 2x error). pccr applied s=0.9846, with an anchor MAD of 6.4 % over 289 keyframes. (b) |s-1| > 0.10 fails the whole session. (c) orient refuses when the camera-down alignment is < 0.7, and the cloud then stays in Omega's frame. (d) _ratio switches each keyframe's estimator on pixel counts (>= 50 / >= 100). Margins today are wide: |s-1| = 1.5 % vs 10 %, alignment 0.977-0.998 vs 0.7. omega-10 (markers) and M-05 (replace-OFF) do not cover these decisions.

map_worker.py:2499  if _dev > _vmax: raise RuntimeError("scale VERIFICATION FAILED ...")
log: '[scale-align] ✅ metric scale s=0.9846 applied (source=da3)'; '[orient] ... (mean alignment 0.977)'
fix_idea: In chunked-metric mode, pass the residual through decide_change: bootstrap the trimmed median over keyframes with a fixed key, apply only if the 95 % CI excludes 1, >= 5 keyframes judge and |log s| >= 2x its measured error, otherwise identity, declared. Record the verify and align margins in scale_diagnostics.json. Keep the fail and refuse gates, but report their margins.

Nothing can flip. Running the residual through decide_change would ADD an apply/skip knife-edge; that is a policy question for the user, not a determinism defect. (b) and (c) are hard bars, but the finding itself shows margins of 1.5 % vs 10 % and 0.977-0.998 vs 0.7, so they cannot flip on negligible differences. (d) In _ratio, the <50 px fallbacks need fewer than 50 pixels in near∩top-10%-conf of a full depth map (tens of thousands of pixels), which is unreachable in practice, and the <100 valid-pixel None only skips a frame.
skeptic_correction: What remains is a policy point, not a determinism one: in chunked-metric mode the verifier's residual s is applied unconditionally rather than under the user's significance rule. Its bits only propagate upstream variance.

On this node the relevant kernels were verified bit-identical (see checked_clean). Nothing pins or records these versions, so an env upgrade changes the keyframes silently. f0f4-14 covers OpenBLAS only for the gauge.

title: Frame extraction leaves no completion record, so a backend restart or a reconstruction started during extraction measures a truncated video
mechanism: _extract_video_frames_sync writes frames/{idx:06d}.jpg one by one, non-atomically, in a backend executor thread. Its progress lives only in the in-memory _video_extract_state. A backend restart or kill mid-extraction leaves a partial frame set, and possibly a truncated last JPEG, which cv2/libjpeg decodes with a 'Premature end' warning instead of failing. After the restart extract_progress reports 'idle' with the on-disk count, so the session looks complete. The pipeline start never checks _video_extract_state (it is referenced only at main.py:1729-1829). The UI hides the hammer only through client state: App.tsx clears extractingSessions on a fetch error, and a page reload loses it. The same video can therefore yield different inventories, which changes I0 ranks, the I1 chain and everything downstream.
fix_idea: Extract into a temporary directory and rename it to frames/ atomically on success, writing frames/manifest.json (video sha256, frame count, per-frame sha256) last. Have the intake refuse a frames/ directory without a complete manifest, and have the pipeline start refuse a session whose extraction is in progress.

title: Card memory and identity are read from nvidia-smi's FIRST GPU, not from the device DA3 actually runs on
mechanism: total_vram_gb(), free_vram_gb() and card_name() take splitlines()[0] of an nvidia-smi query. nvidia-smi lists every GPU in PCI order and ignores CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. torch uses its own visible-device ordering (FASTEST_FIRST by default). On a multi-GPU node, the focal probe, the I3 window size and the da3_vram.json cache key can describe a different card from the one that runs DA3. Window sizes, and so K, the walk and the chunk plan, would then depend on which GPUs are installed and visible. Dormant on today's single-GPU pod.
fix_idea: Read the identity and total memory in-process from the device that will run the job (torch.cuda.get_device_properties(current_device) with name, total_memory, uuid), through repro.card_identity. Fail if CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES does not resolve to exactly one device.

title: The same JPEG frames are decoded by two different JPEG libraries whose versions are never recorded
mechanism: I0, I1, F4 and da3_process_res read frames through cv2.imread, which uses OpenCV's bundled libjpeg-turbo 3.0.3 (IMREAD_GRAYSCALE decodes luma directly). The DA3 focal probe and the I3 windows read the same files through Pillow 12.0.0's own libjpeg-turbo (vendor/depth-anything-3/src/depth_anything_3/utils/io/input_processor.py:300, Image.open(...).convert('RGB')). Each decoder is deterministic for its version. But an upgrade of either package changes the pixels one part of the pipeline sees while the other part stays the same, and no artifact records which decoder produced the inputs. intake-04 covers the encoder and video decoder only.
fix_idea: Include the cv2 and Pillow versions and their libjpeg-turbo builds in repro.environment_record(), stamp the intake and DA3 artifacts with it, and pin both packages in the env lock. Alternatively, store frames losslessly (PNG) through one pinned decoder used by every reader.

title: vLLM runs with prefix caching on, compile-time kernel benchmarking, and no batch invariance, so each answer depends on the engine's history
mechanism: build_argv starts `vllm serve` with only model/port/dtype/len flags, so vLLM 0.19 defaults apply. (1) Prefix caching is on. Every understanding call shares the same system+prompt prefix (text comes before the image in types.Message.to_openai). The first call in an engine lifetime computes that prefix fresh. Later calls, and every call on an engine that was already warm from the chat, a previous scan or an earlier Autosegment, reuse KV that was computed under a different prefill shape. A warm engine and a cold engine therefore produce different logits. Greedy decoding then flips near-ties, which changes phrases, which changes the SAM3 prompts. (2) Inductor compiles with combo_kernels plus benchmark_combo_kernel, which picks kernels by timing. The result is cached in /root/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache, outside /workspace, so a pod restart recompiles and may pick other kernels. (3) VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is never set. In 0.19 its batch-invariant matmul is installed only for sm_80/89/100: the current A100 would get it, the A6000 (sm_86) used before would not. The card the VLM ran on, and the vLLM/torch/flash-attn versions, are not recorded in vlm_analysis.json.

Each request is then computed alone, a pure function of its tokens on a fixed card and stack. Write into vlm_analysis.json the serve argv, the vLLM/torch/flash-attn/transformers versions, the card name and compute capability, and the weights sha256. Verify by replaying the same N calls twice on a cold engine and twice on a warm one and comparing bytes. Optionally cache each request→response keyed by sha(weights, versions, argv, card, request JSON), so a re-run reuses the exact answers.

The engine log shows enable_prefix_caching=True, seed=0, benchmark_combo_kernel True, and compiled graphs loaded from /root/.cache/vllm. /root is on the container overlay, so a pod restart recompiles. 583 log samples read 'Prefix cache hit rate: 59.9%'. batch_invariant.py:938-941 installs the batch-invariant mm only for sm_80/89/100. The current card is an A100 (8.0). No version or card stamp is written into vlm_analysis.json.

Chunked-prefill splits therefore also change with the card. Pinning --max-num-batched-tokens, as the fix proposes, removes this too.

title: Other clients (chat, background session intel) share the engine during a VLM stage and can restart vLLM during SAM3
mechanism: The pipeline's own VLM calls are sequential, but nothing reserves the engine for them. (a) The /spatial_qa route restarts vLLM whenever it is down and does not check for a running pipeline (only the warmup path checks `busy`). It launches _session_intel_when_chat_up(sid, False), which polls is_alive for up to 900 s and then runs ensure_session_analyses (describe_scene). If the next queued job starts vLLM within that window, the two share the engine. ensure_service has no lease. (c) Nothing reserves the engine during the VLM stage or the caption pass.

title: Session vocabulary is reused under a stamp that omits the VLM prompt, model and keyframes, and a reused run silently drops the SAM3 fallback prompts
mechanism: autoprompt_concepts.json is reused whenever `derived_under == signature`. The signature holds only vlm_sampling, max_sam3_prompts, understand_cover and GROUPING_VERSION. It does not include: the understanding prompt (the per-session override saved in output/autosegment.json by the Autosegment window), the merge prompt and merge_* keys, sam3_fallback_max, the keyframe list and its content, the model weights and vLLM version, or the code. title: SAM3 merges new masks into the previous run's seg_masks.npz / segmentation.json, and the mask→cloud match keeps the previous instances
mechanism: Neither the SAM3 stage nor run_segmentation resets the mask store. Per-stage cleanup runs only in replace mode, and replace mode wipes everything anyway. A Replace-OFF Reconstruir or any Autosegment (force=True, replace=False) therefore writes into the old store. Raw ids 1..k of the new first category equal existing ids, so they 'keep their ID, overwrite masks' and take the new label, while the old run's masks of that id in frames the new run does not write stay in the npz (keys are 'kept as stored'). The result is mixed old/new masklets. Genuinely new ids start above the old max_existing_id/id_high_water, and colours are offset by len(existing_instances). Then _match_and_save_result_locked merges `prev_instances` whose ids are not in the new result back into segmentation_result.json. Run 2 on the same input ≠ run 1.

Line 3754: `merged = [inst for inst in prev_instances if inst["id"] not in new_ids]`. main.py:7752: `_force, replace = True, False` (Autosegment).
fix_idea: Have the SAM3 stage write a fresh store into a staging dir (empty npz/json, ids from 1) and swap it in atomically at the end. Drop the incremental merge with prev_instances on the pipeline path; keep upsert only for the interactive Segmentation Manager. Stamp the store with sha(prompt list, keyframes, SAM3 checkpoint, thresholds, code).

It reuses colliding raw ids ('keep its ID, overwrite masks') and appends with keep=existing_mask_keys. Ids and colours are offset from the old store (id_high_water, color_offset=len(existing_instances)). sam3_worker never resets the store, and _cleanup_stage_outputs runs only when replace is on (pipeline_manager.py:866), which wipes everything anyway. _match_and_save_result_locked (3716-3759) keeps prev_instances whose ids are not in the new result and carries their captions over. The SAM3 worker calls run_segmentation, and run_segmentation calls _match_and_save_result, because cleaned_cloud.ply exists at SAM3 time in the current stage order.

title: Per-object ShapeR captions are kept or carried from earlier runs by instance_id+label, and failures are filled in by later runs
mechanism: caption_session_objects skips every instance that already carries a source='object' caption ('kept'), and refresh is never set in the pipeline. carry_object_captions copies an old object caption onto any instance with the same (instance_id, label) after a re-projection. instance_id is a counter that a re-segmentation reassigns (semantic-04), so a different object can inherit a stale caption. A caption that failed (service did not come up, timeout, empty answer) leaves the concept caption, and the next run fills it in. The final segmentation_result.json therefore depends on how many runs happened and which calls failed in each.

fix_idea: On the pipeline path, caption every instance (refresh=True) or reuse only through a cache keyed by sha(the exact crop bytes sent, prompt, model/vLLM stamp). Remove the carry-by-id. When the service is unavailable or a call fails, fail the step and declare it; do not leave a mixed state for the next run to complete.

mechanism: Greedy decoding sometimes enters a repetition loop, and a last-bit logit difference decides whether it does. (a) understand_frame returns None, so all of that frame's objects are lost to the SAM3 vocabulary. (b) merge_synonyms logs 'nothing parseable — kept as is', so NO synonym is merged. A request exception (600 s timeout, HTTP error, prompt+max_tokens over max_model_len) is swallowed the same way. (c) The caption is cut at 256 tokens. Whether the merge happens at all for 134 prompts is decided by a single token.

Server log: `[merge] '*' (134 phrases): nothing parseable — kept as is` → `0 merged`. 33 of 2181 phase1.understand calls on 2026-10-05 ended `length` at 2048 (`1998 call(s) ...; 33 answer(s) did not parse`). consolidate_prompts.py:253-256 `except Exception as e: ... kept as is` / `if d is None ...: continue`.

Then remove the cliff in the simplest way: salvage every complete JSON object of a truncated answer (detector.py already does this for detections) and record finish_reason and the number of entries salvaged per call in the census. A failed request fails the stage instead of being 'kept as is'.

title: Integer cutoffs on VLM-derived counts change the merge strategy, the prompt list and the prompt text
mechanism: (1) `len(phrases) <= merge_max_phrases_per_call (400)` selects ONE whole-list merge call, otherwise one call per head-noun family; one phrase more or less switches between two merges that give different groupings. (2) The SAM3 prompt bound keeps `phrases[:150]` ranked by proposal count; ties at the cut are broken by first-seen keyframe order, so a single call's answer moves a name in or out. (3) scene_type is the Counter.most_common winner over ~2000 free-text answers and is pasted into every merge prompt, so a one-vote flip changes the prompt text of the merge.

mechanism: The Autosegment window saves a VLM-prompt override in output/autosegment.json, and every later VLM pass of the scan uses it, including a later Reconstruir with replace OFF. With autoprompt.reuse_vocabulary, autoprompt_concepts.json is reused whenever `derived_under` matches, but that signature holds only vlm_sampling, max_sam3_prompts, understand_cover and GROUPING_VERSION. It leaves out the understanding prompt (an edited prompt runs all the VLM calls and is then discarded in favour of the old list), the keyframe list (a resumed reconstruction with other keyframes reuses the old list), the served model and weights, and the code. A VLM run after a SAM3-prompt edit reuses the old list again and silently drops the human_validated edit. The first derivation is itself nondeterministic (orchestration-07), and the cache then freezes whichever result came first. Both files also carry wall-clock fields.
evidence: session_builder.py:364-368 `signature = {"vlm_sampling": asdict(vcfg), "max_sam3_prompts": ..., "understand_cover": ..., "grouping": GROUPING_VERSION}`; :450-465 the list is reused when `_prev.get("derived_under") == signature`; :175-176 `vlm_prompt_for(self.output_dir)`; autosegment.py:67 `doc["vlm_prompt_saved_at"] = time.strftime(...)`, :106 `doc["prompt_edited_at"] = ...`.
fix_idea: Treat the prompts as explicit, stamped run inputs. `derived_under` becomes repro.stamp of the understanding-prompt text, the keyframe list with frame hashes, the served model identity (orchestration-07), vlm_sampling, grouping and the code version. An edited SAM3 list also replaces autoprompt_concepts.json, so there is one source. Record the prompt hashes in vlm_analysis.json and the census, and move the timestamps to a log outside the compared artifacts.
skeptic_reason: The reuse signature (session_builder.py:364-368) holds vlm_sampling, max_sam3_prompts, understand_cover and GROUPING_VERSION only. The prompt (from vlm_prompt_for, :175), the keyframe list, the served model and the code are not in it. Reuse is gated only on `derived_under == signature` (:450-458), and autoprompt.reuse_vocabulary is true. autoprompt_concepts.json is not in STAGE_OUTPUT_FILES[VLM] and survives every resume and Autosegment. set_sam3_prompts writes into vlm_analysis.json, which the VLM stage overwrites. autosegment.py:67/111 and session_builder.py:143 stamp wall-clock times into the files.

title: Certification has two launchers that differ in process, environment, config and steps
mechanism: The pipeline runs certify_session in a spawned worker (certify_worker): loops config from the boot copy, correction config from a fresh read, followed by the object captions. Closing the Segmentation Manager runs auto_run, which calls certify_session in a THREAD OF THE SERVER process. That path has the server's environment (random hash seed, server thread pools, no vLLM handover), uses the boot config for both loaders, runs outside the pipeline queue, and skips the captions. /api/segmentation/refresh likewise re-matches the masks inside the server process instead of in the SAM3 worker. The same session certified through the two paths can produce different bytes.
evidence: main.py:6838-6840 `_cert_loop.run_in_executor(None, _certify_api.auto_run, session_id, _cert_loop)`; certify/api.py:126-127 `acta = certify_session(_session_dir(ctx), operator="auto", log=_log)`; certify_worker.py:126-131 `certify_session(session_path, cfg=cfg, ...)` followed by `_caption_objects`.
fix_idea: Keep one launcher. auto_run and the refresh's matching enqueue a pipeline job (kind certify / projection) through pipeline_manager, with the frozen config and the deterministic environment. The server process never runs stage code.
skeptic_reason: /api/segmentation/refresh (main.py:6833-6840) runs certify api.auto_run in an executor thread of the server process when certify.auto_after_segmentation is true (it is). auto_run calls certify_session(_session_dir(ctx), operator='auto') with cfg=None, so both loaders read the server's import-time cfg, with no captions and outside the queue (certify/api.py:107-131). The pipeline path spawns certify_worker with the job's boot copy for loops, a fresh read for correction and precision, and runs _caption_objects afterwards.

title: Viewer-load floor re-levelling flips on a fixed 1 cm / 0.5 deg bar applied to an unseeded RANSAC fit
mechanism: auto_if_needed chooses between 'leave it' and 'rewrite the display frame and every OBB' with `tilt < 0.5 deg and |height| < 1 cm`. Both are invented numbers, applied to a plane from fit_plane_ransac (Open3D segment_plane, unseeded; f5f6-05 covers the primitive) on a seeded 200k subsample of the floor instance. A floor whose fitted height moves around 1 cm between fits is re-levelled on one load and not on the next. Which floor candidate is used also depends on the bars _FLOOR_MIN_SUPPORT_FRAC 0.05, _FLOOR_MAX_MINOR_TILT_DEG 25 and _FLOOR_DOMINANT_FRAC 0.30, and on a lowest-height argmin among eligible candidates.
evidence: main.py:2946 `already = tilt_deg < 0.5 and abs(height) < 0.01`; main.py:2733-2735 the three floor bars; reconstruction/geometry/primitives.py:231 `pcd.segment_plane(...)`.
fix_idea: Apply the user's rule: re-level only when the measured height or tilt is significant at 95 % (bootstrap the plane over resampled floor points, with at least 5 judges) AND at least 2 x its measured error; otherwise change nothing. Per orchestration-10, it never runs as a side effect of loading.
skeptic_reason: main.py:2946 hardcodes `tilt_deg < 0.5 and abs(height) < 0.01`. The plane comes from fit_plane_ransac → Open3D segment_plane (unseeded; primitives.py:231) on a seeded 200k subsample. Candidate eligibility depends on the 0.05 / 25° / 0.30 bars (main.py:2733-2735, segmentation.floor_level) and on a lowest-height sort, with the remembered id overriding all of it. A fit whose height or tilt moves across 1 cm or 0.5° between loads flips the decision between 'no-op' and 'rewrite the display frame, every OBB and the store'.

title: Autosegment prompts are written to disk at save time, not carried by the job: in-flight and queued jobs read, overwrite or wipe them by timing
mechanism: POST /api/autosegment writes autosegment.json and vlm_analysis.json right away. It takes no lock and never refuses: busy is 'shown, never blocking'. The job that later runs carries only the stage set, so its VLM and SAM3 stages read whatever is on disk when they start. (a) A save while another job of the same scan sits between its VLM and SAM3 stages changes that job's SAM3 prompts. (b) Since e6a5520 an Autosegment may queue behind a Reconstruir of the same scan. If that Reconstruir has segment ON, its VLM stage rewrites vlm_analysis.json and the user's human_validated SAM3 edits are lost before the Autosegment runs. If it has replace ON, _wipe_outputs_for_replace deletes autosegment.json and vlm_analysis.json. (c) Both files are written with plain write_text (not atomic) while a stage may be reading them, and load_autosegment / sam3_prompts silently return {} or [] on a parse error. The prompts the run uses therefore depend on click timing and queue order.
fix_idea: Make the prompts part of the job. The Autosegment command carries the exact VLM prompt and SAM3 list, start_pipeline writes them into the job's frozen run inputs (with the frozen config from orchestration-03), and the stages read them from there and stamp their hash into vlm_analysis.json and the census. The save endpoint writes atomically and refuses while a job of that scan is queued or running. A stage fails on an unreadable prompt file instead of defaulting.

title: Object captions from an earlier run are kept with no stamp: any instance already carrying source=='object' is skipped
mechanism: caption_session_objects puts an instance in `kept` whenever shape_caption.source == 'object' (refresh is never passed from certify_worker). The correction edits segmentation_result.json in place and keeps the fields (correction/invalidate.update_instance_store), so an Autosegment of {certify} alone, or any certify re-run, inherits captions written by an earlier vLLM. Those may come from another served model or launch flags (orchestration-07), another `views` count, another caption prompt or another code version. A fresh run would describe them again and get different bytes.
fix_idea: Stamp each object caption with the hash of its inputs (mask keys of its views, view count, prompt text, served-model identity, code version) and keep it only when the stamp matches, otherwise describe the object again. Or have the certify stage always describe from scratch (refresh=True), since captions are part of its product.

title: A failed SAM3 mask→cloud projection is non-fatal: the stage goes green with whatever result the cloud stage left (on a resume, the old masks)
mechanism: After SAM3 the worker re-projects the masks (map_segmentation_to_cloud). Any exception there (memory, a corrupt npz, a lock problem) is logged as 'mask→cloud mapping failed (non-fatal)' and the stage succeeds. segmentation_result.json, classification.npy, scene_r.db and the octree are then whatever was on disk before. On a resumed Reconstruir that is the cloud stage's projection of the PREVIOUS run's masks (orchestration-01a). Otherwise it is nothing, and certify runs with geometric revisits only. The per-object TSDF crop (:230) and the cloud stage's Potree build (cloudcompy_worker.py:461-463) are tolerated the same way. Whether the deliverable carries this run's segmentation therefore depends on a transient failure.
fix_idea: A failure of a step that produces part of the stage's deliverable fails the stage, with the reason. Remove the non-fatal wrappers around map_segmentation_to_cloud and the octree build. The SAM3-carved TSDF meshes go out of the pipeline (they read a leftover scene.glb anyway, orchestration-01d), or their failure also fails the stage.

title: When CUDA is not visible to the SAM3 worker, the configured SAM 3.1 silently becomes SAM 3.0 on CPU
mechanism: load_model branches on torch.cuda.is_available(). With version 'sam3.1' and no CUDA, which can happen through a CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES inherited from the launcher, a driver or context failure, or a busy card refusing a context, it only logs a warning and builds Sam3VideoPredictor (3.0) on CPU, a different model with different thresholds. The stage then segments with the wrong model and still succeeds. Which model produced the masks depends on the process environment, not on config.
fix_idea: A configured version is a requirement: if version == 'sam3.1' (or any CUDA build) and CUDA is unavailable, raise and fail the stage. Record the built version, checkpoint sha256 and device in segmentation.json and the census (repro.environment_record).

title: Wall-clock fields inside the certification and segmentation deliverables make them byte-different on every run
mechanism: These are outside the epoch artifacts covered by f5f6-11. certify_acta.json carries started_at (time.strftime) and correction.elapsed_s. The concept and object shape_captions in segmentation_result.json and vlm_analysis.json carry `generated` = datetime.now() (session_builder.py:143, object_captioner.py:231). The census carries per-prompt `seconds` (segmentation/pipeline.py:661). autosegment.json and vlm_analysis.json carry vlm_prompt_saved_at / prompt_edited_at. Identical inputs therefore never give identical bytes for these files.
fix_idea: Keep wall-clock and durations out of compared artifacts. Write them to a run log or a separate *_timing.json excluded from the reproducibility comparison, and use repro.stamp (input + code + config hashes) as the only identity inside the deliverables.
